g: Intersex or non-binary (in passports and identification documents).
(UK film certificate, dated) Suitable only for those aged sixteen or (later) eighteen years and over.
(originally movie rating) Obscene; adult; pornographic; XXX.
Any mark that looks like that letter, such as a mark made by a person who cannot read or write in lieu of a signature.
An unknown quantity or unknown value.
Let X represent the forecast traffic flow in 20 years’ time.
(fandom slang) Used between the names of two characters to denote a ship, particularly in anime, manga, and video games.
(music) Used in place of and in artist collaborations.
Taska Black x DROELOE, Steve Aoki x Lauren Jauregui, etc.
(sometimes humorous) An unknown or unspecified number of.
(physics) A hypothetical elementary particle that couples quarks to leptons, analogous to the W boson and Z boson, but corresponding to a new type of force predicted by the Georgi–Glashow model.
(genetics) A mammalian sex chromosome: in the XY sex-determination system, cells of females typically have a pair of X chromosomes, while cells of males typically have an X and a Y.
(idiomatic) An unknown or hard-to-define influence; a factor with unknown or unforeseeable consequences.
(idiomatic) A special talent, ability or quality or its indefinable cause.
(astrophysics) The proportionality constant which converts CO emission line brightness to molecular hydrogen mass.
A symbol composed of two perpendicular lines (✗), especially when representing negation or lack of verification.
(idiomatic) One will find what one is looking for under an obvious sign for it.

(biology) A cluster of neurosecretory cells located in the eyestalks of crustaceans; it acts as a primary endocrine center that synthesizes and releases hormones regulating functions like molting and growth.
(transitive) To cross out with a series of the letter X, or with scribbles or lines.
(computing, informal) To close a window (typically by clicking a button marked with an X symbol).
When you have selected your desired settings, X out of the window and return to the document.
A prize, usually a multi-million dollar monetary one, offered for a specific scientific or technological advance.
(Canada, US) A Mexican broadcast station whose signal overpowers those of stations in the United States.
(engineering) A kind of truss shaped like the letter X.
A unit of length (symbol xu) approximately equal to 0.1 picometres, used to quote the wavelength of X-rays and gamma rays.
(idiomatic, sports) The fundamental elements of a play.
(idiomatic, management) The basic delineation of roles in a project.
A kind of flexible, porous aerogel that can form a film.
(analytic geometry) The axis on a graph that is usually drawn left to right and usually shows the range of values of an independent variable.
(physics) An ultrahigh radio frequency, one within the range of 8.0 to 12.0 GHz.

(grammar, X-bar theory) A phrase, or, equivalently, a node in a syntax tree, which consists either of: (1) an adjunct and another X-bar phrase, (2) a head, X, and an optional complement, or (3) a conjunction sandwiched between two other X-bars. The X is a "pro-letter" which can be substituted by le…

(linguistics) A theory that posits a common syntactic structure for different lexical categories. Each phrase (XP) is the projection of a head (X) and may optionally include a specifier (sister of X-bar, daughter of XP), adjuncts (sister and daughter of X-bar) and complements (sister of X, daughter…
(automotive) Any electronic system that replaces a conventional mechanical system in an automobile.
A sandwich consisting of sliced buttered marraqueta bread and other ingredients, typical to the Brazilian state of Amazonas.
A spicy yellow chili pepper used in Yucatecan cuisine.
(film) Strictly reserved for adult viewing; pornographic.
A folding chair with an X-shaped frame.
They took a red-eye flight X-country.
Synonym of D-Day (“the date of any major event planned for the future”).
(algebraic geometry) The direction aligned with the x-axis of a coordinate system.
(informal) Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of the paranormal investigation science fiction television series The X-Files.
Maybe Williams really was in the FBI — some secret X-Filesy part of it.
(music) A hi-hat that is part of a secondary pair of hi-hats on a drum kit placed away from the standard pair of hi-hats.
(typography) The distance between the baseline and midline in a typeface, typically equal to the height of the lower-case letter x.
(mathematics) A root; a zero; a point at which a line crosses the x-axis of a Cartesian grid, where y is 0.
(genetics) A non-linear strand of DNA where certain cruciform binding proteins can compete for binding.
(genetics) Any gene located on the sex chromosomes. Typically, these genes are found on the X chromosome and not on the Y chromosome.

(genetics) Any trait or characteristic whose appearance or absence in a person is determined by a gene on the sex chromosomes. Typically, these genes are found on the X chromosome but not on the Y chromosome.

(computing theory) A theoretical computer that operates on some fundamental data type X. It is a structurally the same as a finite-state machine, but each transition represents the application of a relation of type X→X.
Resembling or characteristic of the X-Men or the media associated with them.
A style of dance performed to drum and bass music.
(patent law) Any of the patents issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office from July 1790 (its founding) to July 1836. They were destroyed in an apparently accidental fire in 1836.
(fandom slang) A fan of the television series The X-Files.
And that’s enough to turn an X-phile into an ex-phile.
(US, military) Any of a series of experimental aircraft and rockets, used to test and evaluate new technologies and aerodynamic concepts.
Denoting a film given an X classification.
I had to put my bags through an X-ray scanner at the airport.

A ray of short-wavelength electromagnetic radiation usually produced by bombarding a metal target in a vacuum. Used to create images of the internal structure of objects; this is possible because X-rays pass through most objects and can expose photographic film.
X-rays are light with a wavelength between 0.1 and 10 nm.
A radiograph: an image made with X-rays.
The doctor ordered some X-rays of my injured wrist.
An X-ray machine, a machine for performing radiography.
(chess) A tactical motif where a piece exerts influence or control over a square, piece, or line indirectly through another intervening piece.
(video games) A cheat that allows a user to see other players, enemies and important objects through walls and other barriers.
(transitive, informal) To take a radiograph of; to obtain an image of using X-ray radiation, especially for the purpose of medical diagnostic evaluation.
Of course there was nothing wrong with my left wrist. They X-rayed the wrong arm!

(transitive, chess) Of a piece, to exert indirect influence, by either attacking, defending, or controlling an opponent's or friendly piece through an intervening piece along a rank, file, or diagonal.
glass (having a high lead content) that resists the penetration of X-rays and gamma rays
(astronomy) An observational branch of astronomy, which deals with the study of X-ray emission from celestial objects.
(astronomy) A binary star system in which one star of the pair is an optically invisible X-ray source.

(analytical chemistry) A technique in which the patterns formed by the diffraction of X-rays on passing through a crystalline substance yield information on the lattice structure of the crystal, and the molecular structure of the substance.
(physics) The scattering of X-rays by the regular lattice of atoms or molecules in a crystal.
(analytical chemistry) The technique of using such patterns to determine that geometry of a crystal, or the arrangements of atoms in a molecule; X-ray crystallography.
(physics) The emission of electrons from a material when exposed to X-rays.
A device that uses soft X-rays to produce images of very small objects.
A type of binary star system containing a regular star orbiting a highly magnetized neutron star.

(physics) Electromagnetic radiation consisting of X-rays, radiation in the X-ray spectrum, of shorter wavelength and higher frequency than ultraviolet and longer wavelength and lower frequency than gamma rays.
(science fiction) Spectacles that allow the wearer to see through solid objects such as walls or clothing.
(analytical chemistry) A device for analyzing the chemical composition of substances using the characteristic spectral lines produced by their interaction with X-rays.
(analytical chemistry) The use of an X-ray spectrometer for chemical analysis.
(physics) The distribution of X-ray photons emitted by a source, as a function of photon energy or wavelength.
A luminous celestial object that emits a major portion of its radiation in the form of X-rays.
An X-ray pulsar, a rotating neutron star that sweeps an X-ray beam toward Earth.
(astronomy) An instrument that detects X-rays originating from outside the Earth's atmosphere.
Pristella maxillaris, a fish with a highly transparent body.
The therapeutic use of controlled doses of X-rays.
A device that produces X-rays by directing energetic electrons into a metal target.
The dentist aimed the X-ray tube at my mouth to find the cavity.
(literally) A vision into the X-ray portion of the light spectrum, enabling visibility through certain solid matter.
(fiction, by extension) The ability or superpower to see through most or all solid objects as if they were transparent.
(video games) A hack allowing players to see enemies behind walls or other solid objects.
A circle in the middle of a shooting target's bullseye used to determine the winner in the event of a tie.
The distance from a person's lower back to the soles of their feet, measured from a sitting position with legs outstretched; used for sizing recumbent bicycles and ultralight aircraft.
(fandom slang, rare) An original character created by a fan to represent how they imagine themselves as an X-Men character.
A simple stool having an X-shaped frame, often one that folds
A pair of flat or curved stretchers, on a chair etc., that often have a knob at the intersection
A convention whereby Esperanto’s circumflex accents (ĉ, ĝ, ĥ, ĵ, ŝ, ŭ) are replaced by an x after the non-diacriticked letter (cx, gx, hx, jx, sx, ux), for convenience of typing.
(computer science) A data structure based on the R-tree, used for storing data in many dimensions.
An aircraft wing design with two wings making an X form in the horizontal plane.

A pattern commonly found in a sudoku grid where the only possible locations for a number, or a pair, are uniquely in only two rows and two columns. Diagonals drawn between these four cells would form a symmetrical X.
(grammar) One of a group of fundamental English auxiliary or modal verb forms.
A device that plots a two-dimensional graph of the relationship between variables.
prefix used for CCITT-ratified (UN) international telecom standards on e-mail
Used as a placeholder for an unknown or variable meridiem.
